text:
alex: Heads up — the onboarding guide's `curl` sample is missing the Authorization header; ran it in staging and got a 401.

alex: Repro (copied from page):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

alex: We should show the `-H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY'` form or an `export REDWOOD_KEY=...` example. Who owns the onboarding doc right now? :eyes:

jess: I can pick this up. Quick question — do we prefer showing the env var approach or an inline header example?

mike: Env var + example header both. Example pattern:
```bash
export REDWOOD_KEY=sk-xxxxx
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Less chance of accidental token paste.

sam: Also recommend adding a tiny troubleshooting note: if you see 401, include the header or check env var. Maybe include the minimal 401 response body for clarity so customers know it's auth and not a runtime error.

jess: I'll open a micro-PR with: (1) add env var + header snippet, (2) add a one-line 401 troubleshooting note, (3) small codeblock showing expected 401 JSON. Planning to send in ~30m.

docs-bot: Created issue #4523: "onboarding: curl sample missing Authorization header" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/4523 :white_check_mark:

alex: Awesome, thank you — happy to review. Ping me in the PR and I'll sanity-check staging.

jess: Thanks! I'll tag @eng-oncall in the PR for a quick smoke test after merge. :hand:

sam: If you want, I can drop a tiny unit test in the docs CI that runs the `curl` snippet against the staging mock (sanitized) so we catch regressions.

jess: That would be great but not necessary for this tiny fix. Filing follow-up to add snippet smoke checks after this lands.

alex: Solid. Closing the loop here — will watch issue #4523.
